mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the federal funds rate increased by more than 0.25% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a strengthening labor market, which historically correlates with increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the unemployment rate dropped by more than 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in a month signals increased demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances where housing starts increased by more than 5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month indicates a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it signals a slowdown in economic activity.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 55% of the instances where industrial production decreased by more than 1% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 1%) signals accommodative monetary policy, which typically supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative more than 50% of the time when the federal funds rate is below 1%.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a simultaneous increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals strong consumer demand and labor market health, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases & UNRATE decreases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional mechanism where a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% in a month during a period of low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2%) signals a healthy labor market without inflationary pressure, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a simultaneous increase in industrial production (INDPRO) and a decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.1% in a month signals increased economic activity supported by accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases & FEDFUNDS decreases > 0.1% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where both conditions are met.
